## Overview

Muse Spark MXFP4 on ROCm at TP > 1: for eager prefill batches of >= 1024 tokens, compute the MoE down projection column-sharded from a second, row-resharded copy of `w2`, so the per-route `[T, top_k, H]` reduce-scatter before the post-expert norm is replaced by much smaller gathers.

## Claims

- **Prefill latency**, TP8 + DSpark on 8×MI355X, single request: TTFT −12% at 2k tokens, −25% at 8k, −26% at 16k, and −26% for a burst of 4 × 8k.
- **Serving**, random 8k in / 1k out: output throughput +13% / +15% at concurrency 32 and +17% / +14% at 16, mean TTFT −24% to −25% at 16 and 32, mean TPOT −12% / −13% at 32 (two independent A/B sessions).
- **Memory cost: +15.9 GiB of weights per GPU (TP8), so the KV cache shrinks by 10%** (6.35M -> 5.72M tokens with `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.90`). The startup log prints the cost. **`VLLM_ROCM_MUSE_MOE_COLUMN_SHARDED_DOWN=0` turns it off** and gives the memory back to the KV cache. It is also off automatically under EP, at TP1, and for the BF16 layers.
- **Accuracy**: GSM8K unchanged (paired exact McNemar p = 0.34). Batches below 1024 tokens are bit-identical; larger prefills change at BF16 rounding level (see Details).
- No change to core files: everything is in `vllm/models/muse_spark/amd/`, plus one env var in `vllm/envs.py`.

## Validation

**Configuration**

| | |
|---|---|
| Hardware | 8×MI355X |
| Image | `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:muse-spark-open` (Python code replaced by the tree under test) |
| Model | `amd/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-Quark-MXFP4`, TP8 |
| Draft | `Inferact/Muse-Spark-Open-DSpark`, 7 speculative tokens |
| Baseline | the same tree without this PR, same machine, same arguments |

Serve command (AMD Day 0 recipe):

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_MUSE_MOE_REDUCE_DTYPE=bf16 VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 \
VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=LBHNC AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN_SHORT_QUERY_3D=1 \
NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=lo GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=lo NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 \
vllm serve amd/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-Quark-MXFP4 --served-model-name musespark \
  --tokenizer-mode hf --config-format auto --load-format safetensors --generation-config vllm \
  --language-model-only --dtype bfloat16 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_FA \
  --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-seqs 64 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --enable-chunked-prefill \
  --reasoning-parser musespark1x --tool-call-parser musespark1x --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","model":"Inferact/Muse-Spark-Open-DSpark","num_speculative_tokens":7,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block","enable_adaptive_verification":false,"attention_backend":"ROCM_AITER_FA"}'
```

Serving sweep: one warm-up (`--random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 256 --num-prompts 16 --max-concurrency 8 --seed 7`), then two runs per concurrency `C`, `R` = 1, 2, averaged:

```bash
vllm bench serve --backend openai --endpoint /v1/completions --model musespark \
  --tokenizer amd/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-Quark-MXFP4 \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 0.0 \
  --request-rate inf --ignore-eos --temperature 0 \
  --num-prompts $((4 * C > 16 ? 4 * C : 16)) --max-concurrency $C --seed $((1000 * R + C)) \
  --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl --metric-percentiles 50,90,99
```

Single-request TTFT: K concurrent `/v1/completions` requests with fresh random token-id prompts of L tokens, `max_tokens=1`, `temperature=0`. We take the wall time until all K finish and report the median over n bursts (the first burst is dropped). The cases are (K, L, n) = (1, 2048, 12), (1, 8192, 16), (1, 16384, 8) and (4, 8192, 6). Prefix caching is off, so each prompt is a full prefill.

**TTFT and memory** (one A/B session; `6c2549be42` with and without this PR):

|---|---:|---:|---:|
| TTFT 2k, median ms | 114.6 | 100.8 | −12% |
| TTFT 8k | 354.4 | 264.8 | −25% |
| TTFT 16k | 722.2 | 536.4 | −26% |
| 4 × 8k burst | 1401.9 | 1034.8 | −26% |
| model weights, GiB per GPU | 82.36 | 98.30 | +15.9 |
| KV cache, tokens | 6,350,664 | 5,717,661 | −10.0% |

**Serving sweep** (8k in / 1k out). These sessions ran on an earlier base, `0626d646d0`. Its `vllm/models/muse_spark/amd/` is identical to that of 6c2549be42, and the single-request TTFT A/B on that base agreed with the table above (8k: −27% in both sessions). Sessions 1 and 2 ran on two different 8×MI355X nodes, each with both arms on the same node.

| C | session | out tok/s base -> PR | mean TTFT ms | mean TPOT ms | AL base / PR |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 1 | 198.0 -> 218.6 | 372 -> 281 | 4.71 -> 4.31 | 2.59 / 2.83 |
| 1 | 2 | 212.6 -> 217.5 | 370 -> 276 | 4.35 -> 4.36 | 2.81 / 2.82 |
| 4 | 1 | 484.8 -> 538.2 | 611 -> 493 | 6.73 -> 6.46 | 2.73 / 2.76 |
| 4 | 2 | 508.1 -> 568.7 | 629 -> 496 | 6.39 -> 5.92 | 2.91 / 3.02 |
| 16 | 1 | 1021.3 -> 1199.6 | 1228 -> 925 | 12.88 -> 11.45 | 2.64 / 2.74 |
| 16 | 2 | 1060.2 -> 1210.3 | 1227 -> 919 | 12.34 -> 11.41 | 2.81 / 2.76 |
| 32 | 1 | 1291.8 -> 1459.1 | 2028 -> 1534 | 20.80 -> 18.36 | 2.74 / 2.75 |
| 32 | 2 | 1327.9 -> 1528.3 | 2019 -> 1538 | 20.54 -> 17.80 | 2.79 / 2.85 |

At c1 / c4 the decode steps (< 1024 tokens) are unchanged by this PR. The TPOT and throughput differences there follow the DSpark acceptance length (AL, mean accepted tokens per step, listed per arm), which varies by about ±0.2 between runs. At c16 / c32, prefills overlap decode, so the faster prefill also shortens TPOT.

**Accuracy**

- GSM8K 5-shot (`lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5`, 1319 questions), on `6c2549be42`: strict 0.9462 -> 0.9507, flexible 0.9454 -> 0.9507. Paired on strict: 11 questions are correct only on the baseline and 17 only with this PR, exact McNemar p = 0.34.
- Deterministic outputs, greedy with logprobs on fixed prompts of 45, 1024, 4096, 8192 and 8192 tokens, compared on first-token logprobs (DSpark at TP8 is not bit-reproducible across restarts after the first token, even for the baseline):
  - The 45-token prompt is bit-identical to the baseline.
  - The 1024–8192-token prompts differ from the baseline by 0.004 / 0.17 / 0.22 / 0.19 nats. These values are identical across restarts and across two machines.
  - On `main` (`2d40c0609f`), the first tokens and logprobs are identical to the 6c2549be42 run above (the later tokens vary as noted).
- TP8 + EP8 + DSpark: the path stays off (no startup log line), the KV cache is 6,317,542 tokens in both arms, and the greedy outputs (text and every logprob) are bit-identical between baseline and this PR.

**Tests and checks** on `main` (`2d40c0609f`, 8×MI355X):

- `tests/kernels/moe/test_muse_spark_rocm_column_sharded_moe.py`, together with the existing Muse ROCm tests (`test_muse_spark_rocm_bf16_moe.py`, `test_muse_spark_moe_finalize.py`, `test_muse_spark_router.py`, `tests/models/test_muse_spark_rocm_loading.py`): 113 passed. The new file covers:
  - which deployments enable the path;
  - the column-sharded finalize against `fused_post_expert_finalize`;
  - at TP2 and TP8 with the real MoE shapes (E 256, H 4096, I/TP 512) and T = 1024 to 8192: the bit-exact weight reshard, the routed outputs within the BF16 rounding bound, and the final output against the existing reduce-scatter finalize on every rank.
- `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` on the TP8 + DSpark server above, with 2k / 8k / 16k / 4 × 8k prefills and the greedy prompts: no sync error was raised (all 69 requests succeeded; the check was armed on all 8 ranks).
- CI: the new test file is picked up by the AMD "MoE Kernels" Buildkite step (`pytest kernels/moe`). On those single-GPU MI300 agents, the deployment and finalize tests run, while the MXFP4 multi-GPU test skips: it needs 2 or 8 MI355X (gfx950) GPUs, which CI does not provide. That test was run on 8×MI355X as listed above.

## Details

**Why.** At TP > 1 without EP, each rank holds `w2[E, H, I/TP]`, so its down projection gives a partial sum of every route over all `H` columns. The per-route post-expert RMSNorm needs the full sums, so `MuseSparkTopKWeightAndReduce` reduce-scatters `[T, top_k, H]` before normalizing. At T = 8192 that is 512 MiB in BF16 per layer, the largest collective in a prefill step.

**How.**

- *Weights, at load.* Before the AITER shuffle, one all-to-all turns this rank's `w2[E, H, I/TP]` and its scales into `w2[E, H/TP, I]` (its output rows over the full intermediate dim). The result is shuffled the same way AITER shuffles the regular `w2`, which is kept for decode and small batches.
- *Experts, T >= 1024, eager.* AITER's `_fused_moe_impl` runs as usual, with its `_stage2_override` hook. Stage 1 is unchanged. In the hook, the MXFP4 stage-1 output and its E8M0 scales are all-gathered along the intermediate dim. Each rank's slice is whole 32-element quant groups, so the gathered tensors equal the full-width quantization exactly. The same stage-2 kernel then runs on the resharded `w2` and gives the exact routed outputs `[T * top_k, H/TP]` for this rank's columns.
- *Finalize.* An all-reduce of the per-route sum of squares (`[T, top_k]` fp32, 256 KiB at T = 8192), two Triton kernels for the norm and the top-k weighted sum on the local columns, and an all-gather of `[T, H]`, the same size as the existing all-gather. Per layer at T = 8192, a 512 MiB reduce-scatter becomes about 136 MiB of all-gathers plus 256 KiB of all-reduce. Stage-2 FLOPs and weight bytes are unchanged.
- *Fallback.* Only the FlyDSL stage-2 kernels, which AITER selects for these shapes, are covered. If AITER picks another stage 2 or a one-stage config, the experts run unchanged and the batch takes the existing reduce-scatter. The choice depends only on shapes and AITER's tuning tables, so all ranks agree.
- *Scope.* The path is off at TP1, under EP, for non-SiLU, bias or padded experts, for `H` or `I/TP` not 256-aligned, for AITER without `_stage2_override`, for the BF16 (Triton) layers, and during graph capture. The recipe captures <= 512 tokens, so graphs never reach the threshold. The DSpark draft has no MoE.

**Memory.** The cost is the second `w2`: per MXFP4 layer and rank, 256 MiB of FP4 plus 16 MiB of scales, 15.9 GiB over 60 layers at TP8. There is no extra workspace: the routed outputs reuse 1/TP of the modular kernel's output buffer, and the gathered stage-2 inputs are transient and smaller than the reduce-scatter buffers they replace. A deployment that values KV capacity over prefill latency can set `VLLM_ROCM_MUSE_MOE_COLUMN_SHARDED_DOWN=0`. Keeping only the resharded copy would avoid the cost, but decode runs in CUDA graphs with AITER kernels the hook does not cover, and at small T one all-reduce is cheaper than three collectives. That is left for a follow-up.

**Numerics.** Both paths compute the same products from the same quantized inputs. The baseline rounds each rank's partial sum to BF16 and then reduces the partials in BF16 (`VLLM_ROCM_MUSE_MOE_REDUCE_DTYPE=bf16` in the recipe). This path accumulates the full intermediate dim in fp32 and rounds once. The unit test bounds the difference elementwise by `2^-8 · (Σ|partial| + |sum|)` with a 2× margin. On TP8 the worst element reaches 0.78–0.86 of the bound, which explains the first-token logprob differences above.

**Complexity.** The PR adds 656 non-test lines (High complexity per the checklist). The breakdown:

- `column_sharded_moe.py` (305): the load-time reshard, the stage-2 hook with the activation and scale gathers, the support check, and `all_gather_columns`.
- `ops/column_sharded_finalize.py` (199): the two Triton kernels.
- `muse_moe_runner.py` (+142): the wiring.
- `envs.py` (+10): the switch.

Most of the work reuses existing code: AITER's stage-1 and stage-2 kernels and tuning tables through the existing `_stage2_override` hook (no new GEMM), AITER's custom all-gather, the experts-to-finalize handoff, and the fused norm parameters. Two pieces looked replaceable but were measured and kept:

- `all_gather_columns` (AITER custom all-gather in row chunks) takes 0.49 ms per layer for the three column gathers at T = 8192 on TP8. `tensor_model_parallel_all_gather(dim=-1)` takes 0.74 ms, so switching would cost 15 ms per 8k prefill.
- The two Triton kernels fuse the norm, the weighting and the top-k sum on the local columns. A PyTorch version would make several extra passes over `[T, top_k, H/TP]` per layer, an estimated ~0.4 ms per layer.

The return is −25% TTFT on 8k–16k prompts and +13–15% throughput at concurrency 32, from the largest prefill collective in the model.

- *Finalize.* An all-reduce of the per-route sum of squares (`[T, top_k]` fp32, 256 KiB at T = 8192), two Triton kernels for the norm and the top-k weighted sum on the local columns, and an all-gather of `[T, H]`, the same size as the existing all-gather. Per layer at T = 8192, a 512 MiB reduce-scatter becomes about 136 MiB of all-gathers plus 256 KiB of all-reduce. Stage-2 FLOPs and weight bytes are unchanged.
- *Fallback.* Only the FlyDSL stage-2 kernels, which AITER selects for these shapes, are covered. If AITER picks another stage 2 or a one-stage config, the experts run unchanged and the batch takes the existing reduce-scatter. The choice depends only on shapes and AITER's tuning tables, so all ranks agree.
- *Scope.* The path is off at TP1, under EP, for non-SiLU, bias or padded experts, for `H` or `I/TP` not 256-aligned, for AITER without `_stage2_override`, for the BF16 (Triton) layers, and during graph capture. The recipe captures <= 512 tokens, so graphs never reach the threshold. The DSpark draft has no MoE.

**Memory.** The cost is the second `w2`: per MXFP4 layer and rank, 256 MiB of FP4 plus 16 MiB of scales, 15.9 GiB over 60 layers at TP8. There is no extra workspace: the routed outputs reuse 1/TP of the modular kernel's output buffer, and the gathered stage-2 inputs are transient and smaller than the reduce-scatter buffers they replace. A deployment that values KV capacity over prefill latency can set `VLLM_ROCM_MUSE_MOE_COLUMN_SHARDED_DOWN=0`. Keeping only the resharded copy would avoid the cost, but decode runs in CUDA graphs with AITER kernels the hook does not cover, and at small T one all-reduce is cheaper than three collectives. That is left for a follow-up.

**Numerics.** Both paths compute the same products from the same quantized inputs. The baseline rounds each rank's partial sum to BF16 and then reduces the partials in BF16 (`VLLM_ROCM_MUSE_MOE_REDUCE_DTYPE=bf16` in the recipe). This path accumulates the full intermediate dim in fp32 and rounds once. The unit test bounds the difference elementwise by `2^-8 · (Σ|partial| + |sum|)` with a 2× margin. On TP8 the worst element reaches 0.78–0.86 of the bound, which explains the first-token logprob differences above.

**Complexity.** The PR adds 656 non-test lines (High complexity per the checklist). The breakdown:

- `column_sharded_moe.py` (305): the load-time reshard, the stage-2 hook with the activation and scale gathers, the support check, and `all_gather_columns`.
- `ops/column_sharded_finalize.py` (199): the two Triton kernels.
- `muse_moe_runner.py` (+142): the wiring.
- `envs.py` (+10): the switch.

Most of the work reuses existing code: AITER's stage-1 and stage-2 kernels and tuning tables through the existing `_stage2_override` hook (no new GEMM), AITER's custom all-gather, the experts-to-finalize handoff, and the fused norm parameters. Two pieces looked replaceable but were measured and kept:

- `all_gather_columns` (AITER custom all-gather in row chunks) takes 0.49 ms per layer for the three column gathers at T = 8192 on TP8. `tensor_model_parallel_all_gather(dim=-1)` takes 0.74 ms, so switching would cost 15 ms per 8k prefill.
- The two Triton kernels fuse the norm, the weighting and the top-k sum on the local columns. A PyTorch version would make several extra passes over `[T, top_k, H/TP]` per layer, an estimated ~0.4 ms per layer.

The return is −25% TTFT on 8k–16k prompts and +13–15% throughput at concurrency 32, from the largest prefill collective in the model.

+"""MuseSpark1x ROCm column-sharded MoE down projection.
+
+The finalize kernels are checked on one GPU against the full-width fused
+finalize; the whole path (re-sharded ``w2``, gathered stage2 input, column
+finalize) is checked on 2 and 8 GPUs against the AITER experts followed by the
+reduce-scatter finalize.
+"""
+
+import os
+import sys
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+import torch.multiprocessing as mp
+
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.activation import MoEActivation
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.config import (

+    FusedMoEParallelConfig,
+    RoutingMethodType,
+)

+from vllm.models.muse_spark.common.ops.fused_finalize import (

+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+

+)
+
+
+def _moe_config(
+    *,
+    tp_size: int = 8,
+    ep_size: int = 1,
+    hidden_dim: int = 4096,
+    intermediate_size: int = 4096,
+    activation: MoEActivation = MoEActivation.SILU,
+) -> FusedMoEConfig:
+    parallel_config = FusedMoEParallelConfig(
+        tp_size=tp_size,
+        pcp_size=1,
+        dp_size=1,
+        ep_size=ep_size,
+        tp_rank=0,
+        pcp_rank=0,
+        dp_rank=0,
+        ep_rank=0,
+        sp_size=1,
+        use_ep=ep_size > 1,
+        all2all_backend="allgather_reducescatter",
+        enable_eplb=False,
+    )
+    return FusedMoEConfig(
+        num_experts=256,
+        experts_per_token=8,
+        hidden_dim=hidden_dim,
+        intermediate_size=intermediate_size,
+        num_local_experts=256 // ep_size,
+        num_logical_experts=256,
+        moe_parallel_config=parallel_config,
+        in_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+        max_num_tokens=64,
+        activation=activation,
+        device=torch.device("cpu"),
+        routing_method=RoutingMethodType.MiniMax2,

+    "kwargs,expected",
+    [
+        ({}, True),
+        ({"tp_size": 2}, True),
+        ({"tp_size": 1}, False),
+        # Under EP the MoE runs at tp_size 1 and keeps the full w2 per expert.
+        ({"tp_size": 1, "ep_size": 8}, False),
+        ({"tp_size": 8, "ep_size": 8}, False),
+        ({"hidden_dim": 3072}, False),
+        ({"intermediate_size": 3072}, False),
+        ({"activation": MoEActivation.GELU}, False),
+    ],
+)
+def test_supported_deployments(monkeypatch, kwargs, expected) -> None:
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        column_sharded_moe, "_aiter_supports_stage2_override", lambda: True
+    )
+    monkeypatch.setenv("VLLM_ROCM_MUSE_MOE_COLUMN_SHARDED_DOWN", "1")

+    assert column_sharded_moe.column_sharded_down_supported(config) is expected
+    monkeypatch.setenv("VLLM_ROCM_MUSE_MOE_COLUMN_SHARDED_DOWN", "0")

+
+
+@requires_rocm
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_tokens", [1, 1024])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("tp_size", [1, 8])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("weight_first", [True, False])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("has_weight", [True, False])
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_column_sharded_finalize(
+    num_tokens: int, tp_size: int, weight_first: bool, has_weight: bool
+) -> None:
+    """Each simulated rank holds every route on its column slice; summing the
+    per-rank sums of squares stands in for the all-reduce. With one rank the
+    result is bit-identical to the fused finalize; with more, only the order
+    of the fp32 sum of squares differs."""
+    from vllm.models.muse_spark.amd.ops.column_sharded_finalize import (
+        column_sharded_finalize,
+        route_sum_squares,
+    )
+
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    top_k, hidden, eps = 8, 4096, 1e-6
+    gain_center = 1.0 if has_weight else 0.0
+    routed = torch.randn(num_tokens, top_k, hidden, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    weight = (
+        torch.randn(hidden, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32) * 0.1
+        if has_weight
+        else None
+    )
+    topk_weights = torch.rand(num_tokens, top_k, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32)
+
+    ref = torch.empty(num_tokens, hidden, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    fused_post_expert_finalize(
+        routed, weight, topk_weights, eps, gain_center, weight_first, ref
+    )
+
+    cols = hidden // tp_size
+    shards = [
+        routed[..., r * cols : (r + 1) * cols].contiguous() for r in range(tp_size)
+    ]
+    weights = [
+        None if weight is None else weight[r * cols : (r + 1) * cols]
+        for r in range(tp_size)
+    ]
+    sum_squares = sum(
+        route_sum_squares(x, w, gain_center, weight_first)
+        for x, w in zip(shards, weights)
+    )
+    outs = []
+    for x, w in zip(shards, weights):
+        out = torch.empty(num_tokens, cols, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+        column_sharded_finalize(
+            x,
+            w,
+            topk_weights,
+            sum_squares,
+            hidden,
+            eps,
+            gain_center,
+            weight_first,
+            out,
+        )
+        outs.append(out)
+    got = torch.cat(outs, dim=-1)
+    if tp_size == 1:
+        torch.testing.assert_close(got, ref, rtol=0, atol=0)
+    else:
+        torch.testing.assert_close(got, ref, rtol=1.6e-2, atol=1e-2)
+
+
+# Muse-Spark-Open's MoE at TP8: hidden 4096, 512 intermediate columns per rank.
+_E, _H, _I_PER_RANK, _TOP_K = 256, 4096, 512, 8
+
+
+def _quantize_mxfp4(w: torch.Tensor) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    from aiter.ops.triton.quant import dynamic_mxfp4_quant
+
+    e, rows, cols = w.shape
+    packed, scales = dynamic_mxfp4_quant(w.reshape(-1, cols))
+    return (
+        packed.view(torch.uint8).view(e, rows, -1),
+        scales.view(torch.uint8).view(e, rows, -1)[..., : cols // 32].contiguous(),
+    )
+
+
+def _rel_err(got: torch.Tensor, ref: torch.Tensor) -> float:
+    return ((got.float() - ref.float()).norm() / ref.float().norm()).item()
+
+
+def _run_rank(device: torch.device, num_tokens_list: list[int]) -> None:
+    from aiter.utility.fp4_utils import e8m0_shuffle
+
+    from vllm._aiter_ops import rocm_aiter_ops
+    from vllm.distributed import (
+        get_tensor_model_parallel_rank,
+        get_tensor_model_parallel_world_size,
+        tensor_model_parallel_all_gather,
+        tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce,
+    )
+    from vllm.models.muse_spark.amd.muse_moe_runner import (
+        MuseSparkTopKWeightAndReduce,
+    )
+    from vllm.models.muse_spark.common.layers import (
+        MuseSpark1xRMSNormWithInputScale,
+    )
+
+    rank = get_tensor_model_parallel_rank()
+    tp_size = get_tensor_model_parallel_world_size()
+    generator = torch.Generator(device=device)
+    generator.manual_seed(1234 + rank)
+
+    def randn(*shape: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+        return torch.randn(
+            *shape, device=device, dtype=torch.bfloat16, generator=generator
+        )
+
+    w13_raw, w13_scale = _quantize_mxfp4(randn(_E, 2 * _I_PER_RANK, _H) * 0.05)
+    w2_raw, w2_scale_raw = _quantize_mxfp4(randn(_E, _H, _I_PER_RANK) * 0.05)

+    cols = _H // tp_size
+    for raw in (w2_raw, w2_scale_raw):
+        full = tensor_model_parallel_all_gather(raw.contiguous(), dim=-1)
+        expected = full[:, rank * cols : (rank + 1) * cols]
+        resharded = column_sharded_moe._all_to_all_rows(raw)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(resharded, expected, rtol=0, atol=0)
+    weights = column_sharded_moe.ColumnShardedDownWeights.from_checkpoint(
+        w2_raw, w2_scale_raw
+    )
+    assert weights.w2.shape[1] == cols
+
+    fp4 = torch.float4_e2m1fn_x2
+    w13_scale = e8m0_shuffle(w13_scale.reshape(_E * 2 * _I_PER_RANK, -1)).view(
+        _E, 2 * _I_PER_RANK, -1
+    )
+    w2_scale = e8m0_shuffle(w2_scale_raw.reshape(_E * _H, -1)).view(_E, _H, -1)
+    w13, w2 = rocm_aiter_ops.shuffle_weights(w13_raw.view(fp4), w2_raw.view(fp4))
+    w13.is_shuffled = w2.is_shuffled = True
+

+        hidden_size=_H,
+        eps=1e-5,
+        has_weight=True,
+        is_post_norm=True,
+        zero_centered_gamma=True,
+        post_norm_gain_center_type="one",
+        residual_id=None,
+        output_norm_gain_center_type="zero",
+    ).to(device)
+    torch.manual_seed(7)
+    norm.weight.data.normal_(0, 0.1)
+
+    from aiter import ActivationType, QuantType
+    from aiter.fused_moe import fused_moe
+
+    for num_tokens in num_tokens_list:
+        # Every rank sees the same batch, as under TP.
+        torch.manual_seed(num_tokens)
+        hidden_states = torch.randn(
+            num_tokens * _TOP_K, _H, device=device, dtype=torch.bfloat16
+        )
+        topk_ids = torch.randint(
+            0, _E, (num_tokens, _TOP_K), device=device, dtype=torch.int32
+        )
+        topk_weights = torch.rand(num_tokens, _TOP_K, device=device)
+        flat_ids = topk_ids.view(-1, 1)
+        unit = torch.ones(flat_ids.shape, device=device, dtype=torch.float32)
+
+        partial = fused_moe(
+            hidden_states,
+            w13,
+            w2,
+            unit,
+            flat_ids,
+            activation=ActivationType.Silu,
+            quant_type=QuantType.per_1x32,
+            w1_scale=w13_scale,
+            w2_scale=w2_scale,
+        )
+        ref_routes = tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce(partial.float())
+        out = torch.empty(
+            num_tokens * _TOP_K, cols, device=device, dtype=torch.bfloat16
+        )
+        got = column_sharded_moe.column_sharded_fused_experts(
+            hidden_states,
+            flat_ids,
+            unit,
+            w13,
+            w2,
+            w13_scale,
+            w2_scale,
+            weights,
+            out=out,
+        )
+        assert got.shape[-1] == cols, f"no covered stage2 at T={num_tokens}"
+        # Same quantized inputs and weights, so the paths differ only in
+        # rounding: the reference rounds each rank's partial sum to bf16 (at
+        # most 2^-8 of its magnitude), this path rounds the full sum once. The
+        # bound has a 2x margin for the fp32 accumulation order.
+        own = slice(rank * cols, (rank + 1) * cols)
+        abs_sum = tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce(partial.float().abs())[:, own]
+        diff = (got.float() - ref_routes[:, own]).abs()
+        bound = 2.0**-7 * (abs_sum + ref_routes[:, own].abs()) + 1e-6
+        worst = (diff / bound).max().item()
+        assert worst <= 1.0, f"T={num_tokens}: route diff {worst:.3g}x bound"
+
+        finalize = MuseSparkTopKWeightAndReduce(norm.forward, pre_norm_all_reduce=True)
+        expected = finalize.apply(
+            None,
+            partial.view(num_tokens, _TOP_K, _H),
+            topk_weights,
+            topk_ids,
+            apply_router_weight_on_input=False,
+        )
+        routes = column_sharded_moe.ColumnShardedRoutes(
+            got.view(num_tokens, _TOP_K, cols)
+        )
+        finalize.take_route_output = lambda routes=routes: routes
+        actual = finalize.apply(
+            None,
+            out.view(num_tokens, _TOP_K, cols),
+            topk_weights,
+            topk_ids,
+            apply_router_weight_on_input=False,
+        )
+        assert actual.shape == (num_tokens, _H)
+        err = _rel_err(actual, expected)
+        assert err < 1e-2, f"T={num_tokens}: output error {err:.3g}"
+        # Every rank must hold the same output.
+        first = tensor_model_parallel_all_gather(actual[None], dim=0)[0]
+        torch.testing.assert_close(actual, first, rtol=0, atol=0)
+
+

+    from vllm.config import VllmConfig, set_current_vllm_config
+    from vllm.distributed import cleanup_dist_env_and_memory
+    from vllm.distributed.parallel_state import (
+        init_distributed_environment,
+        initialize_model_parallel,
+    )
+    from vllm.utils.system_utils import update_environment_variables

+    device = torch.device("cuda", rank)
+    torch.accelerator.set_device_index(device)
+    update_environment_variables(

+            "RANK": str(rank),
+            "LOCAL_RANK": str(rank),
+            "WORLD_SIZE": str(world_size),
+            "MASTER_ADDR": "localhost",
+            "MASTER_PORT": str(port),

+    sys.stdout.flush()

+
+
+@requires_rocm
+@pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not column_sharded_moe._aiter_supports_stage2_override(),
+    reason="AITER without fused_moe's stage2 override",
+)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("world_size", [2, 8])
+@pytest.mark.distributed(num_gpus=8)
+def test_column_sharded_down_matches_reduce_scatter(world_size: int) -> None:
+    """Experts plus finalize against the AITER experts and the reduce-scatter
+    finalize, at the batch sizes that take the path in serving."""
+    if not current_platform.supports_mx():
+        pytest.skip("MXFP4 MoE requires CDNA4")
+    if torch.accelerator.device_count() < world_size:
+        pytest.skip(f"requires {world_size} GPUs")
+    from vllm.utils.network_utils import get_open_port
+
+    mp.spawn(
+        _worker,
+        args=(world_size, get_open_port(), [1024, 1031, 2048, 4096, 8192]),
+        nprocs=world_size,
+        join=True,
+    )

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Column-sharded MXFP4 down projection for MuseSpark prefill at TP > 1.
+
+Under TP the experts' intermediate dim is sharded, so each rank's down
+projection (AITER stage2) yields a partial sum of every route over all ``H``
+output columns, and the per-route post-expert norm needs those summed first:
+a reduce-scatter of ``[T, top_k, H]`` per layer. Instead, this path
+
+1. all-gathers stage2's MXFP4 input and its E8M0 scales along the
+   intermediate dim. Each rank's slice is whole 32-element quant groups, so
+   the gathered tensors are exactly the full-width quantization;
+2. runs the same stage2 kernel on a second copy of ``w2`` that holds this
+   rank's ``H / tp`` output rows over the full intermediate dim, which gives
+   the exact per-route outputs on those columns.
+
+The post-expert norm then needs only a ``[T, top_k]`` sum-of-squares
+all-reduce (see ``ops/column_sharded_finalize.py``) and an all-gather of the
+finalized columns. The second ``w2`` costs ``1 / tp`` of the routed expert
+weights per rank in the MXFP4 layers.
+"""
+
+import inspect
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from functools import cache
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm import envs
+from vllm._aiter_ops import rocm_aiter_ops
+from vllm.distributed import (
+    get_tensor_model_parallel_world_size,
+    get_tp_group,
+    tensor_model_parallel_all_gather,
+)
+from vllm.logger import init_logger
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.activation import MoEActivation
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.config import FusedMoEConfig
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+_MX_GROUP = 32

+def _all_to_all_rows(x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """``[E, H, c]`` intermediate slice of every row -> ``[E, H / tp, tp * c]``
+    full intermediate dim of this rank's rows (bytes)."""
+    x = x.view(torch.uint8)
+    tp_size = get_tensor_model_parallel_world_size()
+    num_experts, rows, cols = x.shape
+    rows_per_rank = rows // tp_size
+    send = (
+        x.view(num_experts, tp_size, rows_per_rank, cols).transpose(0, 1).contiguous()
+    )
+    recv = torch.empty_like(send)
+    torch.distributed.all_to_all_single(recv, send, group=get_tp_group().device_group)
+    # recv[r] is rank r's intermediate slice of this rank's rows.
+    return recv.permute(1, 2, 0, 3).reshape(num_experts, rows_per_rank, -1)

+class ColumnShardedDownWeights:
+    """This rank's output rows of ``w2`` in AITER's stage2 layout."""

+    ) -> "ColumnShardedDownWeights":
+        """Re-shard this rank's raw (unshuffled) ``w2[E, H, I / tp]`` and its
+        scales to output rows with one all-to-all each, then shuffle them the
+        way the AITER MXFP4 backend shuffles the regular ``w2``."""

+        from aiter.utility.fp4_utils import e8m0_shuffle

+        w2, w2_scale = _all_to_all_rows(w2), _all_to_all_rows(w2_scale)

+        w2_scale = e8m0_shuffle(w2_scale.reshape(num_experts * rows, -1)).view(

+def all_gather_columns(
+    x: torch.Tensor, out: torch.Tensor | None = None
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """All-gather TP shards ``[n, c]`` along columns into ``[n, tp * c]``
+    (written into ``out`` when given): AITER's all-gather in row chunks that
+    fit its IPC buffer, else RCCL. Eager only."""
+    comm = getattr(get_tp_group().device_communicator, "aiter_ar_comm", None)
+    if comm is not None and not comm.disabled and x.is_contiguous():
+        ca = comm.aiter_ca
+        row_bytes = x.shape[1] * x.element_size()
+        rows = min(x.shape[0], ca.max_size // (ca.world_size * 2) // row_bytes)
+        # AITER needs every chunk, including the last partial one, 16B-aligned.
+        if row_bytes % 16 == 0 and rows > 0 and ca.should_custom_ag(x[:rows]):

+                out = x.new_empty(x.shape[0], x.shape[1] * ca.world_size)
+            for start in range(0, x.shape[0], rows):
+                end = min(start + rows, x.shape[0])

+    """:func:`all_gather_columns` of a 1-byte ``[n, c]`` tensor, moved as bf16

+    gathered = all_gather_columns(x.view(torch.uint8).view(torch.bfloat16))

+def _gather_scales(a2_scale: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """The full-width E8M0 stage2 input scales from each rank's slice: a
+    32-row band's tiles are one contiguous run per rank, and the ranks' runs
+    side by side are the full-width band."""
+    rows, groups = a2_scale.shape
+    gathered = _all_gather_byte_columns(
+        a2_scale.reshape(rows // _SCALE_TILE_ROWS, groups * _SCALE_TILE_ROWS)

+    return gathered.view(rows, -1)

+def _gatherable(a2: torch.Tensor, a2_scale: torch.Tensor | None) -> bool:
+    """Whether the stage2 input is MXFP4 in the layout the gathers assume."""
+    if a2_scale is None or a2.element_size() != 1 or a2_scale.element_size() != 1:
+        return False
+    if not (a2.is_contiguous() and a2_scale.is_contiguous()):
+        return False
+    groups = a2.shape[-1] * 2 // _MX_GROUP
+    return (
+        a2.dim() >= 2
+        and a2_scale.dim() == 2
+        and a2_scale.shape[1] == groups
+        and groups % _SCALE_TILE_GROUPS == 0
+        and a2_scale.shape[0] % _SCALE_TILE_ROWS == 0
+    )

+"""MuseSpark post-expert finalize over a column shard of the routes.
+
+When each TP rank holds every route's output on its own ``H / tp`` columns
+(rather than a partial sum over all ``H`` columns), the per-route RMSNorm only
+needs the sum of squares across ranks: each rank computes its ``[T, K]``
+partial sums of squares (:func:`route_sum_squares`), the caller all-reduces
+them, and :func:`column_sharded_finalize` normalizes, weights and sums the
+routes on the local columns. Same math as ``fused_post_expert_finalize``.
+"""
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.triton_utils import tl, triton
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _route_sum_squares_kernel(
+    x_ptr,
+    w_ptr,
+    out_ptr,
+    K,
+    H,
+    gain_center,
+    stride_xt,
+    stride_xk,
+    stride_out,
+    BLOCK_K: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK_H: tl.constexpr,
+    HAS_WEIGHT: tl.constexpr,
+    WEIGHT_FIRST: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    t = tl.program_id(0)
+    k = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_K)
+    offs = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_H)
+    k_mask = k < K
+    h_mask = offs < H
+    x = tl.load(
+        x_ptr + t * stride_xt + k[:, None] * stride_xk + offs[None, :],
+        mask=k_mask[:, None] & h_mask[None, :],
+        other=0.0,
+    ).to(tl.float32)
+    if HAS_WEIGHT and WEIGHT_FIRST:
+        w = tl.load(w_ptr + offs, mask=h_mask, other=0.0).to(tl.float32) + gain_center
+        x = x * w[None, :]
+    tl.store(out_ptr + t * stride_out + k, tl.sum(x * x, axis=1), mask=k_mask)
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _column_sharded_finalize_kernel(
+    x_ptr,
+    w_ptr,
+    tw_ptr,
+    ss_ptr,
+    out_ptr,
+    K,
+    H,
+    hidden_size,
+    eps,
+    gain_center,
+    stride_xt,
+    stride_xk,
+    stride_twt,
+    stride_sst,
+    stride_out,
+    BLOCK_K: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK_H: tl.constexpr,
+    HAS_WEIGHT: tl.constexpr,
+    WEIGHT_FIRST: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    t = tl.program_id(0)
+    k = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_K)
+    offs = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_H)
+    k_mask = k < K
+    h_mask = offs < H
+    tw = tl.load(tw_ptr + t * stride_twt + k, mask=k_mask, other=0.0).to(tl.float32)
+    ss = tl.load(ss_ptr + t * stride_sst + k, mask=k_mask, other=0.0)
+    x = tl.load(
+        x_ptr + t * stride_xt + k[:, None] * stride_xk + offs[None, :],
+        mask=k_mask[:, None] & h_mask[None, :],
+        other=0.0,
+    ).to(tl.float32)
+    if HAS_WEIGHT:
+        w = tl.load(w_ptr + offs, mask=h_mask, other=0.0).to(tl.float32) + gain_center
+        if WEIGHT_FIRST:
+            x = x * w[None, :]
+    scale = tl.rsqrt(ss / hidden_size + eps) * tw
+    acc = tl.sum(x * scale[:, None], axis=0)
+    if HAS_WEIGHT and not WEIGHT_FIRST:
+        acc = acc * w
+    tl.store(
+        out_ptr + t * stride_out + offs, acc.to(out_ptr.dtype.element_ty), mask=h_mask
+    )
+
+
+def _blocks(K: int, H: int) -> tuple[int, int, int]:
+    block_k = triton.next_power_of_2(K)
+    block_h = triton.next_power_of_2(H)
+    assert block_k * block_h <= 65536, "routes too wide for the single-tile finalize"
+    return block_k, block_h, 8 if block_k * block_h >= 4096 else 4
+
+
+def route_sum_squares(
+    routed: torch.Tensor,
+    weight: torch.Tensor | None,
+    gain_center: float,
+    weight_first: bool,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """``[T, K]`` fp32 sums of squares of each route over the local columns.
+
+    Args:
+        routed: ``[T, K, H_local]`` per-route outputs on this rank's columns.
+        weight: ``[H_local]`` slice of the norm weight, or ``None``.
+        gain_center: Added to ``weight`` (0.0 when unused).
+        weight_first: Square ``x * (w + gain_center)`` instead of ``x``.
+
+    """
+    T, K, H = routed.shape
+    assert routed.stride(2) == 1
+    out = torch.empty((T, K), dtype=torch.float32, device=routed.device)
+    if T == 0:
+        return out
+    block_k, block_h, num_warps = _blocks(K, H)
+    _route_sum_squares_kernel[(T,)](
+        routed,
+        weight if weight is not None else routed,
+        out,
+        K,
+        H,
+        gain_center,
+        routed.stride(0),
+        routed.stride(1),
+        out.stride(0),
+        BLOCK_K=block_k,
+        BLOCK_H=block_h,
+        HAS_WEIGHT=weight is not None,
+        WEIGHT_FIRST=weight_first,
+        num_warps=num_warps,
+    )
+    return out
+
+
+def column_sharded_finalize(
+    routed: torch.Tensor,
+    weight: torch.Tensor | None,
+    topk_weights: torch.Tensor,
+    sum_squares: torch.Tensor,
+    hidden_size: int,
+    eps: float,
+    gain_center: float,
+    weight_first: bool,
+    out: torch.Tensor,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """``out[t] = sum_k tw[t, k] * norm(routed[t, k])`` on the local columns.
+
+    Args:
+        routed: ``[T, K, H_local]`` per-route outputs on this rank's columns.
+        weight: ``[H_local]`` slice of the norm weight, or ``None``.
+        topk_weights: ``[T, K]`` router weights.
+        sum_squares: ``[T, K]`` fp32 sums of squares over all ``hidden_size``
+            columns (:func:`route_sum_squares` all-reduced over TP).
+        hidden_size: The full norm width ``H``.
+        eps: Norm epsilon.
+        gain_center: Added to ``weight`` (0.0 when unused).
+        weight_first: ``rms_norm(x * w)`` when True, else ``rms_norm(x) * w``.
+        out: ``[T, H_local]`` destination.
+
+    """
+    T, K, H = routed.shape
+    assert routed.stride(2) == 1 and out.stride(1) == 1 and topk_weights.stride(1) == 1
+    assert out.shape == (T, H) and topk_weights.shape == (T, K)
+    assert sum_squares.shape == (T, K) and sum_squares.dtype == torch.float32
+    if T == 0:
+        return out
+    block_k, block_h, num_warps = _blocks(K, H)
+    _column_sharded_finalize_kernel[(T,)](
+        routed,
+        weight if weight is not None else routed,
+        topk_weights,
+        sum_squares,
+        out,
+        K,
+        H,
+        hidden_size,
+        eps,
+        gain_center,
+        routed.stride(0),
+        routed.stride(1),
+        topk_weights.stride(0),
+        sum_squares.stride(0),
+        out.stride(0),
+        BLOCK_K=block_k,
+        BLOCK_H=block_h,
+        HAS_WEIGHT=weight is not None,
+        WEIGHT_FIRST=weight_first,
+        num_warps=num_warps,
+    )
+    return out
